title: backtesting
question: What is backtesting?
options: Scoring a model on its training data|Running the code twice|Reversing the time order|Forecasting from past dates using only what was known then, and scoring against what came next
answer: Forecasting from past dates using only what was known then, and scoring against what came next

title: backtesting
question: In a walk-forward backtest, what happens at each fold?
options: The model is refit on everything before the cut and forecasts the next few weeks|The data is shuffled|Only the test set is changed|The oldest data is deleted
answer: The model is refit on everything before the cut and forecasts the next few weeks

title: backtesting
question: Fold MAEs range from 1.27 to 7.67 with mean 4.01. What should you report?
options: Only the best fold|The spread across folds and when the bad folds occur|Only the mean|Only the last fold
answer: The spread across folds and when the bad folds occur

title: backtesting
question: Backtested on the same six folds, how did one-step naive compare with the regression?
options: Naive won five of six folds with lower mean error|Regression won all six folds|They tied every fold|Seasonal naive won
answer: Naive won five of six folds with lower mean error

title: backtesting
question: The three-year battery call was 1 May 2025. Daily capacity first dipped below 80% on 14 May 2025. Measured against that first dip, how far off was the call?
options: 13 days early|13 days late|74 days early|Exactly right
answer: 13 days early

title: backtesting
question: As more data is used, the battery call gets more accurate. What is the trade-off?
options: The model becomes biased late|The warning time left to act shrinks|The data has more gaps|The threshold changes
answer: The warning time left to act shrinks

title: backtesting
question: In a rolling-origin backtest, what happens at each origin?
options: Shuffle the weeks and score a random block|Refit on all 104 weeks and score the last 8|Using only the weeks before it, forecast the next h weeks blind and score them, then move one week on|Score the forecast on the weeks it was trained on
answer: Using only the weeks before it, forecast the next h weeks blind and score them, then move one week on

title: backtesting
question: The NOC needs a month-ahead staff roster. Why can't the one-step regression, which uses last week's real count, make it?
options: Regression cannot forecast tickets|It is too accurate|Four weeks ahead, last week's real count is not known yet|Rosters must use seasonal naive
answer: Four weeks ahead, last week's real count is not known yet

title: backtesting
question: The backtest from every origin showed naive winning one week ahead and the rate seasonal naive winning four to eight weeks ahead. What does the course recommend?
options: Naive for next week, the rate seasonal naive for 4 to 8 weeks ahead|The regression for every horizon|Seasonal naive for every horizon|The rate seasonal naive for next week, naive for later weeks
answer: Naive for next week, the rate seasonal naive for 4 to 8 weeks ahead

title: backtesting
question: It is fine to try several fold sizes and report the one that makes your model look best.
options: True|False
answer: False

title: backtesting
question: Over six folds the mean MAEs were: rate seasonal naive 2.65, naive 3.13, regression 4.01 and seasonal naive 17.8. The rate seasonal naive beat naive in 3 of the 6 folds. Which statement is honest?
options: The rate seasonal naive wins every fold|The regression is best because it uses the most features|Seasonal naive is best because tickets are seasonal|The rate seasonal naive has the lowest mean, but it wins only half the folds against naive, so report the spread
answer: The rate seasonal naive has the lowest mean, but it wins only half the folds against naive, so report the spread
